newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi opens $250 mln power expansion project.
newsitem.headline: Saudi opens $250 mln power expansion project.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Sunday inaugurated a $250 million expansion of a power plant in the capital Riyadh, part of huge projects to meet soaring demand for electricity.
Official Saudi media said the governor of Riyadh, Prince Salman, opened the project, which increases the plant's power generating capacity to 1,580 megawatt (MW) from 1,000 MW.
The government expects peak electricity consumption in Saudi Arabia to reach 23,310 megawatts by the end of the decade, from 17,228 MW in 1994/95.
To meet this, the government is planning to increase power generating capacity to 25,273 MW in the year 2000 from 18,238 MW in 1994/95.
Some 21 billion riyals ($5.6 billion) is earmarked for boosting power generation between 1995 and 2000 and an additional 27 billion riyals for distribution, according to official figures.
Prince Salman told reporters after the opening that Saudi citizens should cut down on electricity use. "The need to rationalise (electricity use) is a main demand...It is a duty."
